# Domia

> Domia is a private network of local voice AIs with a personality, voice, and memory per device. The full speech-to-speech loop — wake word, voice-activity detection, speech-to-text, a local language model, and text-to-speech — runs on the user's own hardware. No cloud audio, no accounts, no telemetry. Devices discover each other over MQTT, talk peer-to-peer over gRPC streaming, and delegate compute by capability: a thin edge node can borrow a stronger hub's speech and language stages while keeping its own identity and voice.

Domia is written in TypeScript on Node.js. Speech inference runs in-process via sherpa-onnx (ONNX Runtime); the language model runs locally via Ollama or llama.cpp. Every engine and model is swappable per device through database-driven configuration — no hardcoded roles, no vendor lock-in. A new Domia boots neutral and receives its purpose from a template (thin edge node, full hub, or anything in between).

Key facts:
- Fully local speech-to-speech: no audio ever leaves the user's network
- A personality per device: character profile, Plutchik-8 emotional state, and memory, all stored locally
- After each conversation turn, a reflection pass extracts facts and mood shifts locally
- Follow-up conversations without repeating the wake word; sessions keep context
- Peer-to-peer mesh: MQTT discovery, gRPC streaming, capability delegation in a star topology
- One hub can serve several spaces in parallel through child-process inference pools
- Skills via the Model Context Protocol (MCP): opt-in, a Domia picks the right tool mid-conversation and calls it; point it at any MCP server, including a Home Assistant one, to control devices
- The Domia Console is a separate local web app for managing a fleet: replay any conversation with its real audio, per-stage latency breakdowns (STT / LLM / TTS / time-to-first-audio), grade interactions and export them as NDJSON for fine-tuning, portable configuration templates, and a live config editor per device
- Roadmap: multilingual support, episodic memory with local vector recall, more local voice engines, a mobile Console companion
- Open source (Apache 2.0), built in public
